rules: PRODUCTION_SPEC §12–§18; flat LIGHT backgrounds only — image A has a black studio background: cut the chip out (rembg) onto paper/lavender/blush/mint, never show the dark frame. Whole real product; 1–3 words; 2-D objects next to the product; watermark below content; logo v5 end card; audio LOCKED (narrate.py + mix.sh). Length 50–58 s.
official_clips: none — NVIDIA blog has no downloadable video; no YouTube/promo clips (reused-content rule)
palette_for_this_video: paper #FAF8F5 main; lavender #ECE8FB name/record beats; mint for science; blush #FBE7E2 not-for-gaming + THE CATCH; ember accent for numbers; NVIDIA-green only as a thin accent on the chip label, never as background
new_objects: coreGrid (compute.js: grid of tiny squares that fills in order, optional counter) and gpuCard (compute.js: flat 2-slot graphics-card silhouette with fans + label slot) — add both to render/kit/OBJECTS.md

scenes.anchor: NVIDIA just put fifty thousand CUDA cores on one GPU.
scenes.image: A Rubin HPC chip (cut out from black bg, rembg), centred 70% width
scenes.object: coreGrid (NEW): tiny square grid fills the chip's die area while a counter rolls 0 → 50,000+

scenes.image: A Rubin HPC chip (cut out from black bg, rembg), slight push-in 105%
scenes.object: questionStamp pops top-right; counter holds at 50,000+

scenes.anchor: It's called Rubin H P C.
scenes.image: A Rubin HPC chip (cut out from black bg, rembg), left 55% width
scenes.object: name label on a leader line from the chip: 'RUBIN HPC'; small 'VERA RUBIN PLATFORM' pill under it

scenes.anchor: NVIDIA showed it at S C twenty-six, the big supercomputing conference.
scenes.image: A Rubin HPC chip (cut out from black bg, rembg), small 40% bottom-right
scenes.object: calendar page flips to 'NOV 16 2026' with an 'SC26' badge

scenes.anchor: And no, it's not for your gaming PC.
scenes.image: A Rubin HPC chip (cut out from black bg, rembg), right 45%
scenes.object: consoleTower (or miniPc) gaming-PC silhouette with a slash across it

scenes.anchor: Your R T X fifty-ninety has about twenty-two thousand cores.
scenes.object: gpuCard (NEW): flat 2-slot graphics-card silhouette labelled 'RTX 5090'; bars: one bar '21,760' fills

scenes.anchor: This has more than double that.
scenes.image: A Rubin HPC chip (cut out from black bg, rembg), right 45%
scenes.object: bars: second bar '50,000+' grows to 2.3× the first; '2.3×' badge pops between them

scenes.image: A Rubin HPC chip (cut out from black bg, rembg), centred 60%
scenes.object: reviewCard used as a 'RECORD' badge stamped onto the chip corner

scenes.anchor: It's built for science, like climate models and engineering simulations.
scenes.image: C collage — crop molecule + lattice tiles only (no EHT tile)
scenes.object: globe spins with small cloud/temperature icons (climate) + bars for 'simulation' load

scenes.anchor: Sounds great, right? Here's the catch.
scenes.image: A Rubin HPC chip (cut out from black bg, rembg), centred 55%, desaturate 30%
scenes.object: crossMark draws in beside the chip

scenes.anchor: There's no price. No memory size. No power figure.
scenes.image: A Rubin HPC chip (cut out from black bg, rembg), left 45%
scenes.object: three cards flip in a column: priceTag '$ ???', ramStick '? GB', battery/gauge '? W' — each gets a slash

scenes.anchor: And you'll wait until twenty twenty-eight.
scenes.image: A Rubin HPC chip (cut out from black bg, rembg), small 35%
scenes.object: hourglass falls next to calendar flipping 2026 → 2027 → 2028

scenes.anchor: By our score? Fifty-five out of a hundred.
scenes.image: A Rubin HPC chip (cut out from black bg, rembg), left 45%
scenes.object: gauge needle sweeps to 55 (cut-off line at 55 marked)

scenes.anchor: Spec! Just barely. For science labs, not gamers.
scenes.image: A Rubin HPC chip (cut out from black bg, rembg), centred
scenes.object: logo v5 end card: k snaps upright; 'SPEC 55' + small 'FOR SCIENCE LABS' pill

scenes.anchor: Be honest. Would you wait till twenty twenty-eight for fifty thousand cores?
scenes.image: A Rubin HPC chip (cut out from black bg, rembg) exactly as frame 1
scenes.object: coreGrid full + counter 50,000+ as frame 1; small '2028?' pill (seamless loop)
